component.name: Corewatch
component.summary: Watch your processor, memory, processes and more

description.p: Corewatch is a native system monitor for Linux. It shows what your computer is doing right now, with a live graph for every resource.

ul.li: Overview: every resource on one page
Processes: sort by CPU or memory, search, and end a stuck program
Processor: total usage, one graph per core, model and frequency
Memory: used, available, cache, buffers and swap
Graphics: usage or clock, video memory and temperature
Disks: activity, read and write speed, and free space
Network: download and upload speed, addresses and Wi-Fi signal
Sensors: temperatures and fan speeds
Battery: charge, time remaining, power draw and health

description.p: It follows the system light and dark style and accent color, and adapts to narrow windows.

screenshot.caption: Sort, search and end processes, with each app's download and upload speed
Total and per-core usage, frequency and CPU sensors
Load, clocks, memory, temperature, power and fan of every graphics card
Activity, speeds and temperature of each drive
Download and upload speed per interface

ul.li: Group by App: one row per app, with the total CPU, memory, graphics and network use of its processes
Graphics card use of each process, for amdgpu, Intel, NVIDIA and other drivers
Process details: command line, program file, start time, disk reads and writes, and network connections, with Suspend, Resume and Lower Priority
Pressure: how long tasks waited for the processor, memory and disks, on the Overview and on each page
Performance and efficient cores are shown apart on hybrid processors
Alerts for high temperatures, full memory or disks, and a process that keeps a core busy, with an option to keep watching in the background
Graph history of 1, 5 or 15 minutes, or an hour, and the battery's charge over the last day
A faster process scan
Corewatch is now in English only
Persian translation, with a right-to-left layout and Persian digits
Keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9 open the pages, Ctrl+F searches the processes, Delete ends the selected one, and Ctrl+? lists them all
Search processes by name or process ID
Users from systemd-homed, LDAP and other user databases are shown by name
A laptop's NVIDIA graphics card can go back to sleep while Corewatch runs
Ending a process never reaches another process that took over its ID
A failing drive or a slow user database no longer holds up the other pages
Smooth graphs pause while the system's Power Saver mode is on
Drive temperatures from UDisks come back when UDisks starts late or restarts
New Overview page with every resource at a glance
New Processes page with app icons and per-process download and upload speeds: sort, search, and end or force-stop a process
New Network page: speeds, addresses, link speed and Wi-Fi signal
Temperatures and fan speeds on the page they belong to, and a Sensors page for the rest
Temperature of each drive on the Disks page
Rewritten Graphics page: every card with its model name, clock speeds, power and fan, NVIDIA cards with the proprietary driver, and sleeping laptop GPUs left asleep
Smooth, continuously scrolling graphs
Preferences: start page or last page, temperature unit, binary or decimal sizes, and bits or bytes for network speeds
New Graphics, Disks and Battery pages
Preferences: color scheme and update speed
A banner tells you when a data source stops answering
Installable with Meson, and available as a Flatpak

description.p: Log file and clearer error reports.
